earliest date a warrant may be filed and recorded
remedies to prevent the filing and recording

establishes: DOR Taxpayer Bill of Rights: 'A Demand Notice includes: A 20-day notice requiring you to either pay the liability or prove reasonable cause for not paying the amount demanded. The statutory authority of DOR to issue a tax warrant. The earliest date a tax warrant may be filed and recorded. How taxpayers may prevent a lien against their property.'
uncertainty: None.
designImplication: For IN, the demand notice should print the earliest warrant date. That gives the player a visible deadline.

claim: An IN warrant is filed with the circuit court clerk of each county where the person owns property, or Marion County if none is known. It may go through the sheriff, who must file within 5 days of issue. Clerks now receive warrants electronically (INcite e-Tax Warrant), and DOR pays the clerk $3 per filing. The judgment includes clerk's costs and sheriff's costs along with the 10% collection fee, so these are passed to the taxpayer.

value.office: circuit court clerk, each county where the person owns property (Marion County if unknown)

sourceDate: Indiana Office of Court Services guide, updated 7/1/2026; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: Courts guide: 'The filing information is sent back to the DOR electronically so DOR staff can send the $3 per filing payment to the circuit court clerk.' IC 6-8.1-8-2(d) (FindLaw): the clerk lists 'The amount of the tax, interest, penalties, collection fee, sheriff's costs, clerk's costs, and fees'.
uncertainty: That the $3 is the 'clerk's costs' charged into the judgment is inferred. The guide says DOR pays it to the clerk.
designImplication: For IN, record per county. The taxpayer's cost is the 10% fee plus small clerk and sheriff costs.

claim: An IN warrant judgment is a lien on all the person's interest in any chose in action and any real or personal property in the county, except negotiable instruments not yet due. It is valid for 10 years from filing and renewable for further 10-year periods by an alias tax warrant. It must first be filed within 10 years after a demand notice could first issue. If DOR misses the demand, filing or renewal deadlines, the liability is extinguished.

value.attachesTo: chose in action and real or personal property in the county, except negotiable instruments not yet due

sourceDate: IC 6-8.1-8-2 as displayed by FindLaw, last updated January 1, 2026; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: IC 6-8.1-8-2(f)(3): 'A judgment obtained under this section is valid for ten (10) years from the date the judgment is filed. The department may renew the judgment for additional ten (10) year periods by filing an alias tax warrant'. (f)(4): if DOR does not timely issue a demand, file a warrant or renew, 'the department shall extinguish the tax liability'.
uncertainty: Statute read on a secondary host.
designImplication: For IN, the lien lasts ten years and can be renewed. A missed renewal wipes the debt, which is a meaningful edge case.

claim: DOR must release an IN warrant judgment once it is fully satisfied, including accrued interest. DOR mails a Satisfaction of Lien to the clerk. No request is needed. No release deadline in days was found. Paying through the sheriff can take up to two weeks to clear with DOR and may carry sheriff service fees. If the filing was in error, DOR must mail a release and an expungement order to the taxpayer and each clerk. It must do so as soon as possible, and no later than 7 days after both determining the error and learning the judgment was recorded.

value.releaseDocument: Satisfaction of Lien (mailed to the clerk)
value.releaseFeeNote: NOT FOUND; sheriff service fees may apply when paying through the sheriff

erroneousFiling.from: later of DOR's error determination and receipt of the recording information

sourceDate: IC 6-8.1-8-2 as displayed by FindLaw, last updated January 1, 2026; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: IC 6-8.1-8-2(g): 'A judgment arising from a tax warrant in a county shall be released by the department: (1) after the judgment, including all accrued interest to the date of payment, has been fully satisfied; or (2) if the department determines that the tax assessment or the issuance of the tax warrant was in error.' (h): 'The department shall mail the release and the order for the warrant to be expunged as soon as possible but no later than seven (7) days after: (1) the determination by the department that the filing of the warrant was in error; and (2) the receipt of information by the department that the judgment has been recorded'. Courts guide: 'When the tax is paid, a Satisfaction of Lien is mailed to the circuit court clerk'. DOR Sheriff's Warrant page (https://www.in.gov/dor/i-am-a/tax-professional/the-collection-process/stages-of-collection/sheriff-warrant/): 'It may take up to two weeks to process before the tax lien is cleared with DOR and may be subject to additional service fees.'
uncertainty: The two-week figure is for payments made to the sheriff. The 7 days applies only to erroneous filings.
designImplication: For IN, release is automatic on payment. An erroneous warrant is not just released but expunged within 7 days, so it leaves no trace.

claim: If DOR determines an IN warrant was filed in error, it mails a release and an expungement order within 7 days. The release must state that the filing was in error. If the judgment is obstructing a lawful transaction, DOR must send them immediately. On the taxpayer's request, DOR mails a copy to each major credit reporting company in each county where the judgment was filed. The commissioner may also expunge warrants in the state's best interest, for example after five years of full compliance or when the warrant is more than ten years old. Expungement may be refused for fraudulent, intentional or reckless conduct. Before filing, the taxpayer can prevent the warrant by showing reasonable cause within the 20-day demand period.

value.process: DOR determination; taxpayer may show reasonable cause within the 20-day demand period

sourceDate: IC 6-8.1-8-2 as displayed by FindLaw, last updated January 1, 2026; accessed 2026-10-11
establishes: IC 6-8.1-8-2(i): 'If the department determines that a judgment described in subsection (h) is obstructing a lawful transaction, the department shall immediately upon making the determination mail: (1) a release of the judgment to the taxpayer; and (2) an order requiring the circuit court clerk ... to expunge the warrant.' (j): 'A release issued under subsection (h) or (i) must state that the filing of the tax warrant was in error.' (q)(1): expunge 'If the taxpayer has timely and fully filed and paid all of the taxpayer's state taxes ... for the preceding five (5) years.'
uncertainty: Statute read on a secondary host. The rules under (p) defining best-interest expungement were not read.
designImplication: For IN, expungement is a real mechanic. A clean five-year record lets old warrants vanish, which rewards later compliance.

claim: No IN source found says a DOR payment plan withholds or releases a warrant, or requires one. Plans through INTIME are available for balances over $100. After a sheriff warrant, the taxpayer may set up a plan of up to one year with the county sheriff, or pay DOR through INTIME. The lien clears only once the warrant is paid.
establishes: DOR Sheriff's Warrant page: 'Pay directly or establish a payment plan (for up to one year) with your county sheriff. It may take up to two weeks to process before the tax lien is cleared with DOR.' DOR Payments & Billing (https://www.in.gov/dor/i-need-to/make-a-payment/): 'You can set up a payment plan if you owe more than $100.'
uncertainty: The relationship between a DOR plan and warrant filing is not documented on the pages read.
designImplication: For IN, keep the warrant independent of plans. A sheriff plan is capped at 12 months.

claim: An IN warrant filed with the county clerk becomes a judgment lien and a public record. Clerks must make warrant information publicly available. DOR names these effects: the warrant appears on a title search, becomes a lien on property across the state, and leads to DOR tax liens on every vehicle title in the taxpayer's name or Social Security number.

stateNamedEffects: becomes a lien on property across the state
DOR places tax liens on all vehicle titles in the taxpayer's name or SSN

establishes: DOR Stages of Collection: 'the information will appear on a ... title search and becomes a lien on your property across the state.' 'A customer ... who has outstanding liabilities that have been filed as a lien in the county clerk's office will have DOR tax liens placed on any and all vehicle titles that are titled in their name and/or Social Security number'. Courts guide: 'circuit court clerks must ensure that tax warrant information is available to the public in some way.'
